criteria.reasoning: The report opens with an identity check: "The prospect is Robert Frederick ('Robert F.') Smith, founder, chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners". It explicitly excludes "the musician Robert Smith of The Cure and former U.S. Senator Robert C. Smith". Everything it attributes to him belongs to the Vista founder.
The report states "Founder, Chairman and CEO of Vista Equity Partners, which he founded in 2000".
The report states "B.S. in chemical engineering, Cornell University (1985); M.B.A., Columbia Business School (1994)", both correct.
The report states "Residence: Austin, Texas", citing the DOJ release and Forbes.
The report gives "Net worth: about $10 billion" as Forbes' March 2026 figure, which is within the $9–13 billion band. The older figures are labelled as prior-year values.
The report identifies "Fund II Foundation, his private foundation (EIN 47-2396669), founded in 2014. He is its founding director and President" and calls it his "Giving vehicle".

The report lists the 2016 Cornell gift as "$50 million (combined, Smith and Fund II Foundation)" and says "Cornell named the Robert Frederick Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering". It notes Vista's $20M + $10M split as an acceptable addition.

The report gives the Morehouse Class of 2019 gift as "$34 million", pledged "At the May 19, 2019 commencement". It adds that "Early press estimates of about $40 million were superseded", correctly treating $40 million as the early estimate.

The report states "$50 million from Fund II Foundation (June 2020) plus $50 million personal gift from Smith (October 2020)" for SFI's HBCU STEM program. It says Cisco's $150 million and Steinbridge's $100 million were "Not his money".

The report names several documented ties. Prairie View A&M "was one of SFI's first nine partner HBCUs"; Texas Southern, Texas College and Jarvis Christian joined in the 2021 expansion; he gave the Huston-Tillotson commencement address on May 10, 2014; and Fund II made a $10,000 donation to Prairie View A&M in 2021.

The report says "No major gift from Smith to a Texas HBCU is on record. Fund II Foundation's only Texas HBCU grant is a $10,000 donation to Prairie View A&M in 2021." It invents no other gift or naming.

The report states that "On October 15, 2020 the DOJ announced that Smith had entered a non-prosecution agreement" over a 2000–2015 offshore scheme. It gives the payment as "more than $139 million in taxes and penalties (about $56 million plus $82 million)".
The report states "He was not charged. He admitted the conduct, agreed to cooperate". It does not claim an indictment or exoneration and does not mention Brockman.

The matter sits under "Red flags (for internal due diligence)". The report advises "Do not raise the matter with Smith or his staff, and keep it out of proposals and talking points. If he raises it, respond briefly and neutrally."
The report gives a capacity of "$25–50 million" and an ask of "$10 million over five years". The ask does not exceed the capacity.

The report's facts match the fact sheet. These include Denver birth and age 63, Vista AUM over $107 billion, Fund II assets of $138.7 million and grants of $5.7 million, the gift amounts and years, the Huston-Tillotson date and the DOJ figures. Where the sheet allows either version (Cornell 2022 at $15M or $25M, the Fund II title), the report stays within those alternatives.
